context_chunks:
<chunk id="US10791298B2::desc::p0056">
A persistent difficulty in perovskite-silicon tandem photovoltaics is moisture- and thermally-driven degradation of the perovskite absorber under damp-heat testing. Known approaches address this only partially and at a cost in manufacturability.
</chunk>

<chunk id="US10791298B2::desc::p0059">

<question>
These passages come from two different applications. Summarise what each one claims about frequency-modulated continuous-wave LiDAR and how they differ, citing the passage behind each statement.
</question>
context_chunks:
<chunk id="US12392653B2::claims::p0001">
1. A coherent optical ranging system, comprising a silicon-photonic optical phased array configured to steer a frequency-chirped beam without a moving part, and a balanced photodetector pair for coherent detection. (Applicant: Robert Bosch GmbH.)
</chunk>

<chunk id="EP3664321A1::claims::p0001">
1. A coherent optical ranging system, comprising a silicon-photonic optical phased array configured to steer a frequency-chirped beam without a moving part, and a balanced photodetector pair for coherent detection, wherein a chirp non-linearity is corrected using a reference interferometer having a fixed delay. (Applicant: Beamforge Semiconductor Co., Ltd.)
</chunk>

<chunk id="EP3664321A1::desc::p0066">
The approach of the present application differs from earlier proposals in that no additional processing step is required to address the cost and reliability penalty of mechanically scanned time-of-flight LiDAR in automotive service.
</chunk>

args.summary: The two applications claim similar coherent FMCW LiDAR systems built around a silicon-photonic optical phased array and balanced photodetector pair, but the Beamforge Semiconductor application (EP3664321A1) adds a chirp-linearization feature not present in the Bosch application (US12392653B2). A description passage within EP3664321A1 further asserts that its approach avoids an additional processing step needed to offset the cost and reliability drawbacks of mechanically scanned time-of-flight LiDAR, which appears to be in tension with its own claim requiring a correction step via a reference interferometer.

key_points.text: US12392653B2, applied for by Robert Bosch GmbH, claims a coherent optical ranging system with a silicon-photonic optical phased array that steers a frequency-chirped beam without a moving part, paired with a balanced photodetector pair for coherent detection.

EP3664321A1, applied for by Beamforge Semiconductor Co., Ltd., claims the same core system (silicon-photonic optical phased array steering a frequency-chirped beam without a moving part and a balanced photodetector pair for coherent detection) but adds correction of chirp non-linearity using a reference interferometer having a fixed delay.
The key difference between the two claims is that EP3664321A1 includes the chirp non-linearity correction limitation, while US12392653B2 does not include this element.

A description passage in EP3664321A1 states that its approach differs from earlier proposals because it requires no additional processing step to address the cost and reliability penalty of mechanically scanned time-of-flight LiDAR in automotive service, which appears inconsistent with the claim's requirement of a chirp non-linearity correction step.

1. <chunk id="EP3550158A1::desc::p0043">

key_points.text: US10762925B2, applied for by Robert Bosch GmbH, claims a coherent optical ranging system with a silicon-photonic optical phased array that steers a frequency-chirped beam without a moving part, plus a balanced photodetector pair for coherent detection.

EP3550158A1, applied for by Beamforge Semiconductor Co., Ltd., claims the same core coherent optical ranging system elements (silicon-photonic optical phased array steering a frequency-chirped beam without a moving part, plus a balanced photodetector pair) but adds correction of chirp non-linearity using a reference interferometer with a fixed delay.

EP3550158A1 also describes that its approach avoids the need for an additional processing step compared to earlier proposals, addressing the cost and reliability penalty otherwise associated with mechanically scanned time-of-flight LiDAR in automotive service.

The key difference between the two applications is that EP3550158A1 adds the chirp non-linearity correction feature via a fixed-delay reference interferometer, which is absent from the claim of US10762925B2.

</question>
context_chunks:
<chunk id="US12094814B2::claims::p0001">
1. A method of training a machine-learning model across client devices, comprising applying per-client gradient clipping to a fixed L2 norm before adding Gaussian noise calibrated to a per-round privacy budget. (Applicant: Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.)
</chunk>

<chunk id="EP3357247A1::claims::p0001">
1. A method of training a machine-learning model across client devices, comprising applying per-client gradient clipping to a fixed L2 norm before adding Gaussian noise calibrated to a per-round privacy budget, wherein client updates are combined under a secure aggregation protocol such that the server observes only the sum. (Applicant: QUALCOMM Incorporated.)
</chunk>

<chunk id="EP3357247A1::desc::p0076">
In contrast to earlier proposals, the disclosed approach obviates the need for an additional processing step to address the accuracy cost associated with noise addition. Such a step is therefore not required in implementations where client data are non-identically distributed.
</chunk>

args.summary: Both applications describe a federated learning method that applies per-client gradient clipping to a fixed L2 norm before adding Gaussian noise calibrated to a per-round privacy budget, but EP3357247A1 (Qualcomm) adds a secure aggregation protocol so the server only sees the summed updates, a feature not present in the Huawei claim. EP3357247A1 also asserts in its description that its approach removes the need for an extra processing step to offset the accuracy cost of noise addition, particularly when client data are non-identically distributed, a benefit not discussed in the Huawei passage.

key_points.text: US12094814B2, assigned to Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd., claims a method of training a machine-learning model across client devices using per-client gradient clipping to a fixed L2 norm followed by addition of Gaussian noise calibrated to a per-round privacy budget.

EP3357247A1, assigned to QUALCOMM Incorporated, claims the same clipping-and-noise approach but additionally requires that client updates be combined under a secure aggregation protocol so the server observes only the sum.

EP3357247A1's description states that, unlike earlier proposals, its disclosed approach removes the need for an additional processing step to address the accuracy cost of noise addition, and that this step is not required when client data are non-identically distributed.

The key difference between the two applications is the presence of a secure aggregation protocol limiting the server to observing only the aggregate sum, which is included in EP3357247A1's claim but absent from US12094814B2's claim.

</chunk>

context_chunks:
<chunk id="US11492131B2::desc::p0031">
A persistent challenge in surface-code quantum error correction is presented by decoder throughput that is insufficient to keep pace with the syndrome extraction rate, resulting in a backlog and destruction of the logical qubit. Conventional approaches address this issue only partially and introduce challenges with respect to manufacturability.
</chunk>

A control system for a quantum processor comprises a real-time syndrome decoder implemented in field-programmable logic. The decoder is configured such that, for a code distance of at least 7, a correction is returned within one surface-code cycle.
</chunk>

<chunk id="US11492131B2::desc::p0037">
The article resulting from the process of Example 1 exhibits a logical error rate per cycle of 1.4e-4 at distance 7. This result is attributed to the use of the configuration described above.
</chunk>
